facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s presented with a new pigmented lesion on his left second toenail
The lesion first appeared 12 months before presentation and was progressively growing
The lesion was asymptomatic
He was otherwise well and denied any fevers or weight loss
dark brown longitudinal pigment band covering the full length of the toenail of the left second digit with corresponding nail thickening over the pigmented band
The pigment was the same width throughout the band and extended to the proximal nail fold
No other nail or skin lesions were found at the time of examination
Bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix with invaginations of the epithelium
No melanocytic lesions observed
Immunostaining negative for S100 and CD34
Intracorneal hemorrhage and adjacent verrucous hyperkeratosis present
Villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate without melanocytic proliferation or keratinocyte atypia

concepts.why: Bland spindle cell proliferation within the nail matrix with invaginations of the epithelium and villous fibroepithelial projections into the nail plate without melanocytic proliferation or keratinocyte atypia are characteristic of onychopapilloma
Dark brown longitudinal pigment band covering the full length of the toenail with corresponding nail thickening is consistent with nail melanonychia
Nail thickening over the pigmented band is a characteristic feature of onychauxis
Verrucous hyperkeratosis present in the nail plate is consistent with subungual keratosis
The absence of melanocytic lesions and negative immunostaining for S100 and CD34 explain the uncovered findings.

rationales.F05: Pigmented band is a common feature of onychopapilloma and nail melanonychia
rationales.F08: Bland spindle cell proliferation is characteristic of onychopapilloma
rationales.F09: Absence of melanocytic lesions rules out nail melanonychia
rationales.F10: Negative immunostaining for S100 and CD34 rules out nail melanonychia
rationales.F12: Villous fibroepithelial projections are characteristic of onychopapilloma
